title: Floating-point subtraction
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Why must floating-point exponents match before the mantissas are added directly?
questions.answer: Because corresponding mantissa bit positions must represent the same scaled place values .
options: Because corresponding mantissa bit positions must represent the same scaled place values .
questions.feedback: Aligning the exponents puts both operands on the same scale before the mantissas are added.

blocks.title: Align before subtracting
blocks.text: Choose a common exponent and use arithmetic right shifts to align the mantissas. Keep any low-order guard bits needed for an exact working result.

blocks.title: Negate the second mantissa
blocks.text: At the chosen working width, invert every bit of B’s aligned mantissa and add 1.

blocks.title: Add the aligned values
blocks.text: Sign-extend both operands to the same working width, add them, and interpret the signed result using the common exponent.

blocks.title: Handle cancellation, zero and range
blocks.text: A small difference may need left shifts and a reduced exponent to become normalised. Equal operands produce zero.
